content.text: : replaces Fe, found in hgb, myoglobin, and other enzymes; allows the transportation of O2 via hgb
: MC product for PO replace therapy
SE: constipation, darkens stool, nausea, epigastric pain
BBW: accidental OD of iron-containing prod = a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children <6yo – keep product out of reach of children
: delivers Fe as ferritin; dissociates upon uptake from the GI tract allowing Fe and maltol to be absorbed separately
: Fe replace product for the tx of Fe deficiency in adults
: hemochromatosis & other Fe overload syndromes; pts requiring repeated blood transfusions
: flatulence, diarrhea, constipation, discolored feces, abd pain/discomfort/distention
: ⍉use if IBD flare = present, danger of iron-overload in children
: released ferric ion = transported by transferrin and incorporated into Hb or storage sites
: dyspnea, hypotension, neurological sxs, N/V, flushing, pruritis
: anaphylactic-type rxns, incl fatalities, have followed the parenteral use of Fe dextran – test dose required
: tx of IDA in chronic hemodialysis pts (>6yr) receiving supplemental EPO therapy
: tx of IDA in CKD, incl nondialysis-dependent pts (w/w.o receiving EPO therapy) and dialysis-dependent pts receiving EPO therapy
: tx of IDA in adults w CKD
: tx for adult pts who either cannot tolerate or have ⍉responded well to PO Fe; iron deficiency anemia (IDA) in adult pts w ⍉dialysis-dependent CKD
: B12 deficiency in several conditions, incl maintenance therapy following IM therapy and HIV, AIDS, and Crohn’s dz
: maintenance therapy of pernicious anemia after normalization of B12 levels w injectable B12
: glycoprotein manufactured thru recombinant DNA technology and has the same actions as EPO

: chemotherapy-induced anemia, anemia assoc w/ CKD, anemia ← zidovudine, pediatric anemia in children undergoing dialysis for CKD, reduction of allogenic blood transfusion in surg (elective, noncardiac, nonvascular) pts @ ↑risk for perioperative transfusion w sig, anticipated blood loss
: CKD (↑BP, HA, arthralgias, nausea), HIV (fever, fatigue, HA, cough, diarrhea, rash, nausea, skin rxns, congestion, dizziness), allergic rxns
: anemia assoc w/ CKD both on & off dialysis, anemia in pts w/ ⍉myeloid malig where anemia = ← the effect of concomitantly administered chemo

: pts treated w ESA and dosed to a target hgb concentration of 13.5 g/dL were @ a significantly ↑risk for serious and life-threatening CV comp (death, MI, hsp for CHF, CVA) compared to pts dosed to a target Hb of 11.3 g/dL – FDA recommends a target Hb in the range 10-12 g/dL and ⍉ to exceed 12 g/dL; pts have an ↑risk of serious CV events and death when these prod are dosed to target Hb > 12 g/dL

: in CA pts w certain tumor types (ie, breast, non-small cell lung, head and neck, lymphoid, cervical), ESAs shortened overall survival and/or ↑the risk of tumor progression or recurr in some clin studies – in pts w CA, use the lowest ESA dose needed to ⍉RBC transfusions and serious cardiovasc and thromboembolic rxns

: use ESAs only for tx of anemia ← concomitant myelosuppressive chemo, and d/c following the completion of a chemo course – pts receiving myelosuppressive chemo should ⍉be treated w ESAs when the anticipated outcome = cure
: antineoplastic agent/antimetabolite: ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor that prevents DNA synth and has been used in chemo regimens
: for use by adults w recurr mod or severe painful crises (≥3 in the preceding 12mo) to reduce the freq of crises and the need for blood transfusions
